Sirajul Huq with Ahmed Ali, Advocates   ------- For the Petitioner. 
M Shamsul Alam, Deputy Attorney-General with SA Hasan Assistant Attorney-General  ------- For the State.
parties:
ASM Abdur Rob  ------- Petitioner 

Vs. 

The State  ------- Opposite Party
full_judgment:
Anwarul Haque Chowdhury, J.: This Rule arises out of an application under section 498 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and is directed against an order dated 31.3.1991 passed by the learned Sessions Judge, Lakshmipur, in Criminal Misc. Case No. 142 of 1991 arising out of Ramgati Police Station Case No. 1 dated 7.5.91 and No. 2 dated 8.5.86 rejecting the prayer for bail. 

 2. Fact of the case is rather a chequered one and it need be stated in some details. In the General Election held in 1986 there arose some incident of assault, hijacking of ballot papers including the Presiding Officer and consequent murder which gave rise to the First Information Report dated 7.5.86 filed with the Ramgati Police Station, Lakshmipur by Abdul Wahed, an independent candidate in that general election held in 1986. It is alleged in that FIR that while the polling at Rabbania Madrasa Centre No. 11 Barakheri Union Parishad was going on the accused petitioner namely, ASM Abdur Rob, a candidate of Jatiya Samajtantric Dal, came along with others being armed with various weapons and by assaulting the voters, the agents, the Presiding and the Assistant Presiding Officers and firing gun shots snatched away the ballot box of the said polling centre and took it to the nearby house of accused Jasimuddin, Chairman and in front of the house of Jasimuddin chairman accused No. 1 namely, ASM Abdur Rob fired from his gun injuring 20/25 persons of whom two namely, Jitendra Kumar Dhupi and Tajul Islam was seriously injured and they died in the hospital immediately thereafter. On the same incident there was another First Information Report filed by Abdur Rab Kanungo, a Revenue Officer and the Presiding Officer of that Rabbania Senior Madrasa Polling Centre and it is to the effect that while the said Abdur Rob was the Presiding Officer of the said polling centre at about 9-00 AM the Chairman of Barakheri Union Parishad being armed with ballam, surki tried to enter into the polling booth forcibly and the Presiding Officer ordered to fire two rounds. At that the men of Jasimuddin ran away and the polling started again. At about 10'clock ASM Abdur Rob came by a blue colour jeep to the polling booth. He stopped his jeep before the house of Chairman Jasimuddin and along with Chairman Jasimuddin and others all armed with lathi, surki, ballam and DBBL gun and pistol entered into the polling booth and by pointing dagger and rifle at the Ansars, ASM Abdur Rob and Jasimuddin, Chairman and others entered into the polling booth and started beating by lathi the Presiding Officer and the Assistant Presiding Officer. The nephew of Chairman Jasimuddin and Rashid assaulted the informant and thereafter they by beating him all the time took him by force to the Chairman's house and detained him there. After some time assistant Emdadul Huq was also taken to Jasimuddin's house and kept in detention. They also took to that house all the materials of the polling centre including the ballot boxes and while they were so locked the accused often came out of the house along with the DBBL gun and the pistol and the revolver and started shooting. The informant could hear the cry of human beings from inside. At one stage in that melee the Chairman Jasimuddin by putting a revolver at the chest of the informant, the Presiding Officer and Upazila Kanongo, forced him to put his signature in some papers and out of fear of life he did it. At 2-30 afternoon people came on the spot and also the Additional Deputy Commissioner (General) along with one Army Major, Officer-in-Charge of the Ramgati Police Station and the Superintendent of Police and they rescued him and his assistant from the custody and also arrested some people and the names of the arrested persons had been mentioned in that First Information Report and it. is further stated that except the DBBL gun other weapons could not be recovered from the spot as the accused took these away before. It is further stated in the FIR that after being released from the house of the Chairman he came to know that by gun shots many person have been injured and out of them Tajul Islam and Jitendra Kumar Dhupi had died. It has been further stated that Noman had taken Tk.780.00 from the pocket of the informant and also his wrist watch. Both these First Information Reports are dated 7.5.86. 

 3. The Officer-in-Charge of the Ramgati Police Station took up investigation of both the cases separately but under the order of Upazila Magistrate amalgated both the cases and after investigation submitted one charge sheet of the two cases against 22 co-accused under sections 147/148/ 150/325/332/342/379/302/34 of the Penal Code except ASM Abdur Rob. 

 4. The said police report was accepted by the learned Upazila Magistrate and the present petitioner has not been sent up for trial by the police in that charge. He was discharged by the Magistrate vide his order dated 25.10.1986. The learned Magistrate thereafter sent the case records to the learned Assistant Sessions Judge, Noakhali and eventually the learned Sessions Judge held the trial in Sessions Case No. 86 of 1986 and after trial acquitted all the accused charge sheeted in that case by his judgment and order, in that double murder case in broad day light, by his judgment dated 25.2.87. 

 5. Four years passed thereafter. On 13.1.91 Jatana Rani Majumder, wife of victim Jitendra in that case lodged another ejahar on the date above mentioned before the SP, Lakshmipur alleging that on 7.5.86 her husband Jitendra, the victim went to the polling centre at about 12-00 noon and at 1-00 PM she came to know from Kamini Kumar Das that the accused petitioner with others came to the polling centre at Rabbania Madrasa. Abdur Rob and his people after heavy firing took away the ballot papers and the Presiding Officer by force to the house of Chairman Jasimuddin from the Rabbania Madrasa Centre Polling Booth and detained him in the house of the said Chairman Jasimuddin. Her husband Jitendra Kuman Dhupi and others went to protest and obstruct in front of the Chairman's house whereupon the petitioner Abdur Rob and Chairman Jasimuddin opened fire indiscriminately from revolvers in their hands, injured seriously two persons, her husband and one Tajul Islam. On hearing that news she along with her relations went to the polling station and after her husband and Tajul Islam was taken to the Ramgati Charitable Hospital. He died there soon. Post-mortem over the dead body of her husband was held on 7.5.86. Thereafter she came to know that a case has been instituted about the murder of her husband but she did not receive any information as to the fate of that criminal case. Thereafter she, being a helpless poor widow, could not take any information from any place. It has been stated by her in that complaint that ASM Abdur Rob was a collaborator of the past regime and for fear of life and safety she could not make any tadbir and whatsoever she made was of no result and it is prayed that the matter be inquired and investigated properly so that she can get proper justice for the murder of her husband and the named person in the First Information Report is named to be ASM Abdur Rob, son of Late Haji Ali Azam Mia of village Bara Bedana known as Char Badam, Police Station Ramgati, District Lakshmipur. 

 8. Mr. Serajul Huq, the learned Advocate appearing in this case for the petitioner, argued the case at length and after taking us through the previous two FIRs, the previous charge sheet which excluded ASM Abdur Rob, the subsequent judgment delivered by the Sessions Judge who discharged all the accused for want of proper evidence and the subsequent FIR filed in 1991 in the month of January by Jatana Rani and the consequent charge sheet submitted by the CID Police and the impugned order rejecting a prayer for bail, submitted the aim and purpose of a supplementary charge sheet is to add further material to the original one which is the pre-requisite of a supplementary charge sheet and the said supplementary having not added anything to previous FIR cannot exist in the eye of law. He has further submitted that in the instant case there was an examination of the gun by ballistic experts and after examining the same the expert was of the opinion that the fired cartridges were not fired from the seized gun and this factum is enough to show that the allegations against the petitioner is a false one. He has further submitted that other accused who had been acquitted in the previous Sessions case stand on the same footing being co-accused with the petitioner ASM Abdur Rob and they having been discharged for want of evidence the said order would be presumed to be an order of acquittal of the present petitioner also as such the present proceeding against the accused petitioner suffers from a legal bar. He lastly submitted that in the instant last FIR the allegation is that of killing by shots from a revolver but in the previous FIR it was a case of killing by gunshot injury which clearly reveals that subsequent prosecution story is a manufactured one. He further submitted that the case which ended in acquittal is inseparably connected with the present case as the incident was the same, the place of occurrence and date was the same the manner was the same and as such the present case though not barred under section 403 it clearly indicates that the allegations are not free from doubt on a similar allegation previously the present petitioner was not even charge sheeted and not even faced trial the present criminal proceeding against the accused is a mockery of trial and therefore he has every chance of acquittal in this case and consequently he should be enlarged on bail and hence the order refusing bail by the learned Sessions Judge is not sustainable in law. 

 9. Mr. Shamsul Alam, the learned Deputy Attorney-General also submitted quite a lengthy argument. It is his submission that in the instant case accused ASM Abdur Rob is a powerful person as in spite of specific allegation in the FIR and also in the second FIR that two murders occurred in that polling and the presiding officer giving details of the occurrence in making the FIR yet ASM Abdur Rob was declared elected over the two dead bodies. It shows how powerful he was. He was very powerful not only to be declared elected in spite of two murders and too powerful not to be included even in the charge sheet in spite of specific allegation that he did the murder in broad day light. Mr. M Shamsul Alam, the learned Advocate in elaborating his contention submitted that the other accused who were acquitted in the instant case before were in fact not in any way connected or implicated in the murder of that two persons and as the police omitted to send the real culprit to trial the case ended in acquittal. Supplementary charge sheet is not barred in law and according to the learned Deputy Attorney-General the matter was further investigated as the police did not get all facts earlier and it caused no error or illegality and after finding a prima facie case as I alleged in the FIR of 1991 filed by Jatana Rani wife of the victim the Police submitted charge sheet against ASM Abdur Rob. He is now facing a trial for double murder and at this stage he should not be enlarged on bail as he would come directly under the embargo as in section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure which provision of law was also taken into consideration by the sessions court below in refusing his prayer for bail and further that the petitioner did influence earlier and he will influence now if released on bail. 

 12. A murder if proved would call for a punishment of death or imprisonment for life. In granting bail the court however shall not go deep into the merits of the case but only to see whether there are prima facie materials on record-to show that the prosecution had been able to make materials strong enough to show that there is a possibility that the accused has complicity in the alleged offence of murder and be punished. 

 13. In the instant case we have examined the allegation as in the FIR made in 1991 and also the allegation of murder as made in the previous FIR where the main accused is named to be ASM Abdur Rob. We have examined the judgment passed by the learned Sessions Judge. Lakshmipur and we find from there that the learned Sessions Judge in examining the bail matter discussed the previous acquittal of other accused and the court observed that non-submission of charge sheet against the petitioner ASM Abdur Rob by the police was without any valid reason and found that there were specific allegation that the petitioner ASM Abdur Rob had direct complicity in the two murders all along and finding that there is specific allegation  against the accused petitioner now the court after finding that the petitioner is a very powerful man in the locality and finding that there is a possibility of influencing the witnesses found it not desirable that he would be released on bail. 

 14. We find that there is substance in the finding that the accused petitioner is a very powerful man in his locality and, in fact, he was not even charge sheeted earlier and in exempting him from trial the police mentioned even no ground for doing so. We having examined the order of refusal to grant bail by the court of sessions in the light• of observation made by the court below and also in the light of the attending facts and circumstances of the case find that there are in fact specific allegation against the petitioner ASM Abdur Rob in this case of double murder though previously he was not even charge sheeted and he was not even put on trial. It is the prosecution that is to prove the charge against him beyond all reasonable doubts which is the basis of all criminal trial but at this stage we do find that there is a strong prima facie case against the petitioner and if proved he may be sentenced to death or imprisonment for coming with the embargo as under section 497 of the Code of Criminal Procedure and we do not find any illegality committed by the court below in refusing the bail of petitioner ASM Abdur Rab, also on the ground that he is capable of interfering with the witnesses and the proceeding and we having found no other compelling reason, after examining the matter in great detail at this stage, to enlarge the petitioner on bail, we restrained from making any kind of observation whatsoever touching the merits of the case as it should prejudice the accused at the trial. The Rule is thus discharged.
